newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metro Pacific says 1996 net up 64 percent.
newsitem.headline: Metro Pacific says 1996 net up 64 percent.

text.p: Philippine conglomerate Metro Pacific Corp said on Thursday it posted a 64 percent rise in net profit in 1996 to 843.9 million pesos as its diversification efforts began to show a return.
The company, a unit of Hong Kong's First Pacific Co Ltd, said in a statement that equity in net earnings of affiliated companies grew 207 percent in the year to 485.5 million pesos.

These companies included the Bonifacio Land Corp, which has won the right to develop a former military camp in the heart of Manila and posted its maiden profits in 1996, real estate company Landoco Inc, mobile phone firm Smart Communications Inc and PDCP Development Bank, it said.
"Our strategy of diversification and investing for the long term in growth industries is now beginning to bear fruit," said company president Napoleon Nazareno. "We are delighted with the results."

"The focus of the group has changed over the recent years as significant investments have been made in property development, telecommunications and in banking to provide a balance to our established consumer products and packaging subsidiaries," he added.

"The diversity of these interests has enabled Metro Pacific to produce strong overall growth in net profit for the year and provides a foundation to further substantial earnings growth in the future."
The company said all subsidiaries, except packaging firm Steniel Manufacturing Corp, showed strong earnings growth in 1996.
"Steniel experienced severe difficulties during 1996 as a result of over-capacity in the market and the effect of the fall in world paper prices," Nazareno said.

He said a reorganisation of the company was progressing well and was "anticipated to return the corrugated operations of Steniel to profitablity while maintaining its position as the leader in the industry.
Metro Pacific also said earnings per share increased in 1996 to 25.49 centavos from 18.89 centavos.
A Reuters poll of local brokerage houses last month had predicted Metro Pacific would record net profit of 704 million pesos in 1996 and about 1.1 billion pesos this year.
Nazareno made no earnings forecast for 1997 but said: "We are confident that the group will continue to develop strongly in 1997 and in succeeding years."
